 Selangor to review development approvals to ensure flood mitigation measures
 06-Nov-2026, 14:47 06 Nov 2026, 14:47 Bernama Share MB Amirudin Shari says developers may be required to build temporary water retention facilities, while illegal structures in flood-prone areas will be demolished.
 Selangor menteri besar Amirudin Shari during a press conference after inspecting areas affected by overflowing water at UiTM’s Puncak Alam campus in Kuala Selangor today. (Bernama pic) 
 KUALA SELANGOR : The Selangor government will review previously approved development projects to ensure that adequate flood mitigation measures are in place, particularly in high-risk areas. 
 Menteri besar Amirudin Shari said the review would include imposing requirements for developers to build temporary water retention facilities to reduce flood risks.
 “I will request a review of all approvals we have granted, and include a requirement for developers to build temporary water retention facilities.
 “We do not want them to carry out the work in a shoddy or substandard manner,” he told reporters after inspecting a retention pond at Universiti Teknologi Mara’s Puncak Alam campus today.
 Amirudin said the state government had also identified several other factors contributing to flooding in areas such as Johan Setia, Parit Mahang, Bukit Kuching and Bukit Hijau.
 These include vandalism involving embankments under the Sungai Buloh 1 flood mitigation scheme, where structures were lowered below their original specifications, as well as water overflowing from the West Coast Expressway.
 “We will take action against illegal operations in the area, and several demolition exercises will have to be carried out.
 “These demolitions are necessary to gazette the sites as water catchment areas or floodplains. Two locations have already been identified for this purpose,” he said.
 The process will be carried out by the district and land office in collaboration with the local authorities.
 On a mosque that frequently experiences flooding despite not being near a river, Amirudin said the state would discuss with its management the possibility of raising the building or relocating it to a more suitable site.
 He said the mosque was in a low-lying area that received excess water from Sungai Subang.
